text:
Three Nanooks student-athletes named to CSC Academic All-America At-Large Teams
A. F. Burns
The Nanooks had two male student-athletes and one female student-athlete named to the 2025-26 College Sports Communicators (CSC) Academic All-America At-Large Teams, according to a July 8 announcement from the university. Lassi Lehti of the Nanooks ice hockey team and Rosie Fordham of the Nanooks Nordic skiing team earned spots on the First Team, while Ben Dohlby of the Nanooks Nordic skiing team garnered Third Team honors.
Lehti, a senior goalie from Espoo, Finland, secured Academic All-American honors after a standout season between the pipes for the Blue and Gold, appearing in 25 games for the Nanooks while posting a 13-9-3 record with a 2.41 goals-against average and a .919 save percentage. The goalie had nine 30+ save performances this past year, and one 40-save performance at Wisconsin, good for a career high. His performances earned him Independent Goalie of the Year honors, UCHC MVP recognition, and helped lead the Nanooks to an independent championship with a pair of 30+ save outings in Alaska's two UCHC wins over Stonehill and Lindenwood. In the classroom, he posted a 4.00 GPA while studying Business Administration.
Joining him as a First Team recipient is Rosie Fordham, a redshirt senior from Sydney, Australia. After representing her country in the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympic Winter Games, she returned to collegiate competition with two podiums at the RMISA West Region Championships—third in the 7.5k classic and nearly winning in the 20k freestyle by just under half a second. Two weeks later at NCAA Championships she won both events: "winning the 7.5k classic by over a minute and the 20k freestyle by nearly 28 seconds en route to a pair of NCAA Championships." In addition to her success on ski trails, Fordham held a 3.92 GPA while studying mathematics.
Ben Dohlby—a junior from Pewaukee—garnered Third Team honors after his season on Nordic ski trails paired with his academic achievements: "He earned a Third Team selection after...a successful season on trails paired with...a 3.59 GPA while studying Mechanical Engineering." Dohlby grabbed fourth-place finishes at Utah Invitational before competing at U23 World Ski Championships; he returned for NCAA Championships where he notched fifth place in his final race—the men's NCAA Skiing NC Championship—and earned First Team All-American honors in that event for the second consecutive season.
